subject: Performance evidence & scaling commitments for Globex multi-tenant endpoints
messages:
From: Michael O'Neil <m.oneil@globex.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@globex.com, ops-team@globex.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: performance evidence for multi-tenant endpoints

Ben —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our SRE team need concrete evidence on how Redwood behaves under our mixed traffic profile (chat + instruction + embeddings) before we proceed to the pilot. Specifically we need:

- Peak sustained throughput (tokens/sec) for a 2k context model and a 4k context model under mixed QPS profiles.
- 99th percentile token latency at QPS targets (10, 50, 200) and at 95th percentile load.
- How request-level KV/prefix caching affects tail latency for repeated conversational sessions.
- Graceful degradation behavior and the fallback matrix when a dedicated pool is saturated.
- Runbook for how Redwood will reproduce the tests and artifacts we can audit (traces, kernel selections, hardware profile).

Can you send a concise evidence pack (test methodology, raw traces, a short runbook, and a signed statement of scaling commitments)? Procurement would like a doc bundle by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael O'Neil
Head of Infrastructure
Globex Corporation

Attachment: globex_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael O'Neil <m.oneil@globex.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: performance evidence for multi-tenant endpoints

Michael —

Appreciate the detailed ask and the timeline. We're on it. Quick outline of what we'll provide by EOD Monday: 

1) Short methodology doc explaining workload synthesis and test harness (latency/throughput instrumentation).
2) Raw artifacts: token-level traces, kernel selection logs, and the condensed CSV traces you can run down in-house.
3) A one-page runbook for reproduction (hardware, software stack, sequence of steps).
4) Signed commitments: target 99th percentile token-latency and throughput ranges and fallback behavior at each load tier.

Karthik — looping you in to own the technical artifacts and the runbook; can you confirm we can reproduce Globex's mixed profile in our traffic sandbox and include a stress plan that exercises cache hit/miss scenarios?

Lauren — FYI for procurement and commercial commitments; we will include a short commitment letter (SLA hinge points + acceptance criteria) for their procurement team.

Michael — will follow up with the evidence bundle and a short recording of the test run. Anything else we should include?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Michael O'Neil <m.oneil@globex.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: performance evidence for multi-tenant endpoints

All —

Confirmed: we can reproduce Globex's described mixed traffic. Short clarifications so the delivered artifacts are actionable:

- Models under test: we'll run two representative open models (7B lower-precision and 13B quantized) with the same sequence-length distributions you provided.
- Hardware: NVIDIA H100 (A100 fallback profile in the runbook). We'll include the exact driver, CUDA, and Triton/runtime versions.
- Workload synthesis: chat sessions (60% of requests), short instruction completion (30%), and embedding calls (10%). We'll include separate runs with and without prefix/KV caching enabled.
- Load tiers:
  * Tier A: 10 QPS sustained for 60 mins (pilot baseline)
  * Tier B: 50 QPS sustained for 30 mins (expected production)
  * Tier C: 200 QPS sustained for 20 mins (stress envelope)
- Metrics recorded: per-token latency histogram (us), per-request end-to-end latency, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, kernel-choice timeline, and cache-hit ratio.

Artifacts we'll attach: runbook_globex_v1.pdf, redwood_globex_perf-evidence.zip (contains traces and kernel logs), trace_samples_globex.csv (condensed traces), and a short notes.txt with interpretation. We'll also include a short video (recording link) showing the dashboard during the Tier C run.

On fallbacks: we will include evidence of our configured fallback rules (model-variant swap, cross-region fallback, and queue-delay thresholds) and an event timeline showing graceful degradation (no request drop, queued delay and eventual model swap). We'll provide a deterministic recipe to reproduce the fallback state.

Action items: Karthik to produce artifacts by Mon 11/9 EOD PST and Ben to assemble the procurement commitment letter.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: runbook checklist (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael O'Neil <m.oneil@globex.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, procurement@globex.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: performance evidence for multi-tenant endpoints

Michael —

Attached is the evidence pack we promised. Highlights up front:

- Tier B (50 QPS) 13B quantized run: sustained 38k tokens/sec aggregate, 99th-per-token latency = 290ms, end-to-end 99th-per-request = 420ms.
- With KV/prefix cache enabled for sessionized traffic, observed 99th-per-token latency improvement of ~28% on recurrent sessions.
- Tier C stress run triggered model-variant fallback after 120s of sustained 200 QPS; no request loss, median queue delay peaked at 520ms pre-fallback. Post-fallback 99th-per-token latency returned to within 1.3x of Tier B values.
- Artifacts include kernel selection timeline useful for correlation and the GPU utilization traces.

Attachments included in the zip: per-token-traces.jsonl, kernel-selection.log, gpu-utilization.csv, trace_samples_globex.csv. Also attached: runbook_globex_v1.pdf (repro steps + exact environment), and proposal-commitment-letter.pdf (SLA hinge points and acceptance tests).

Next step: Lauren, please confirm the commercial language aligns with our standard EOLs and the acceptance test window. Michael — if procurement needs any changes to the commitment letter, flag them here and we'll route through legal.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_globex_perf-evidence.zip (contains 4 files), runbook_globex_v1.pdf, proposal-commitment-letter.pdf

From: Michael O'Neil <m.oneil@globex.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@globex.com, ops-team@globex.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: performance evidence for multi-tenant endpoints

Ben / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clearly annotated artifacts. We spot-checked the trace_samples_globex.csv and kernel logs; the kernel-choice annotations are helpful for our HW team. A couple quick asks before procurement signs off: 

1) Can you add a short appendix to the runbook listing the exact kernel versions and a checksum for the per-token-traces.jsonl (so our audit can verify artifact integrity)?
2) Procurement requests one minor edit to the proposal-commitment-letter: clarify the acceptance test window (we'd like 10 business days for run verification after delivery).

If you can attach those by EOD Thursday we'll route to legal. Otherwise looks good and we appreciate the explicit degradation recipe — that was very useful.

Best,
Michael
Head of Infrastructure, Globex Corporation
